In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-196-030)
recent_violations.inspector_comments: A STRUCTURAL ENGINEERS' REPORT IS REQUIRED FOR THE LARGE REAR STRUCTURE BEHIND 3923-25 S. KEDZIE. THIS 1 STRORY SPACE CURRENTLY CONTAINS AN UNLICENSED PPA EVENT SPACE. THIS (APPROXIMATELY) 50'X50' ADDITION WAS CONSTRUCTED WITHOUT PLANS, PERMITS OR LICENSED PERSONELL. THE NORTH MASONARY WALL STRUCTURE WAS VISABLE (THE OTHER 3 WALLS WERE CLAD WITH SIDING OUTSIDE AND DRYWALL INSIDE). THIS MASONARY WALL MAY NOT HAVE A STRUCTURAL FOOTING AND IF IT DOES, IT'S DEPTH AND CONDITION COULD NOT BE DETERMINED. THE GENERAL CONDITION OF THIS REAR STRUCTURE APPEARS TO HAVE BEEN CONSTRUCTED BY UNLICENSED PERSONELL DUE TO THE LACK OF QUALITY (WALLS OUT OF PLUMB, SUBSTANDARD ROOF STRUCTURED WITH UNDERSIZED RAFTER SYSTEM).THIS REPORT IS TO BE BASED ON A COMPLETE EXAMINATION IF THIS REAR ADDITION (WALLS, FLOOR SYSTEM, ROOF SYSTEM). THIS REPORT IS NOT TO BE USED IN LIEU OF ARCHITECTURAL DRAWINGS IN SO FAR AS REPAIRS / UPGRADES TO THIS REAR ADDITION. NO WORK IS TO BE PERFORMED UNLESS / UNTIL A FULL SET OF ARCHETECTURAL DRAWING ARE SUBMITTED AND APPROVED BY THE DEPARTMENT OF BUILDING AND ZONING.14X-1-104.1

recent_violations.inspector_comments: A LICENCED TAVERN AT 3923 S. KEDZIE  HAS BEEN CONNECTED TO THE ADJOINING COMMERCIAL SPACE (3925) BY THE BREACHING OF THE FIRE WALL BETWEEN BOTH SPACES. ALSO, BOTH THE TAVERN (3923) AND THE COMMERCIAL SPACE (3925) HAVE BEEN JOINED TO A LARGE 1 STORY SPACE BEHIND THE 2 FRONT SPACES (3923-25) VIA A BREACH IN THE REAR WALLS OF (3923-3925). ALL OF THESE ALTERATIONS (PARTITION WALLS, ROOF STRUCTURE, ELECTRICAL / PLUMBING PIPING, WIRING AND FIXTURES) WERE PERFORMED WITHOUT ARCHITECURAL PLANS OR PERMITS. THE RESULTING CONFIGURATION CONTAINS, IN ADDITION TO THE ORIGINAL TAVERN (3923) AND ORIGINAL COMMERCIAL SPACE (3925), A BILLIARDS ROOM WITH FIXED SEATING (3925) AND A LARGE PPA SPACE IN THE REAR STRUCTURE BEHIND (3923-25). THIS REAR STRUCTURE CONTAINS A PERFORMANCE STAGE, FIXED SEATING, A DANCE FLOOR AND A FIXED DJ BOOTH WITH SOUND SYSTEM. A LIVE BAND SET UP WITH MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS EXISTS ON THE PERFORMANCE STAGE.THERE ARE NO LICENCES FOR THE (3925) ROOM OR THE PPA SPACE AT THE REAR (3923-25 REAR). THE DOB HAS ISSUED A CLOSURE FOR THE ENTIRE PREMISES.SECTION 14A-4-401.1

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: THE MAIN ROOF MEMBRANE OF THIS BUILDING IS SEVERELY COMPROMISED WITH NUMEROUS AREAS OF WATER INCURSION. THIS ROOF HAS ALLOWED FOR RAIN WATER / SNOW MELT TO ENTER THE INTERIOR FOR A LONG PERIOD OF TIME AS EVIDENCED BY THE LARGE PUDDLES OF WATER ON THE FLOOR FROM A RECENT RAIN EVENT. ALSO, VIRTUALLY 100% OF THE STRUCTURAL ROOF RAFTERS ARE WATER SATURATED AND SEVERELY WOOD ROTTED. AN UNPROFESSIONAL ATTEMPT TO REPAIR THESE VITAL STRUCTURAL RAFTERS HAS BEEN PERFORMED BY NAILING NEW 2"X8" BOARDS INTO THE EXISTING ROTTED / WATER SATURATED RAFTERS. THIS IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE REPAIR AND ACCOMPLISHES NOTHING TO REMEDY THIS DANGEROUS CONDITION. ALL AFFECTED RAFTERS ARE TO BE REPLACED. ALSO, VIRTUALLY ALL OF THE ROOF BOARDS ARE ROTTED / WATER SATURATED AS WELL WITH AREAS WHERE THERE ARE HOLES THROUGH THE ROOF MEMBRANE AND ROOF BOARDS. PLANS AND PERMIT ARE REQUIRED. DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS.SECTION 14X-303.1.1.

THE EXPOSED BRICKWORK BEHIND THE PARGE COAT REVEALS EXTREMELY DEBRADED BRICK WALLS WITH MOST OF THE BRICK MORTAR HAVING ERODED LEAVING WALLS CONSISTING OF LOOSE / SHIFTED / DISPLACED BRICKS. Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
